## Design

### 2026-10-10 – I read through the Blare alarm clock guide and decided what I wanted my clock to be like. Then I picked the components:

**1.67h**

I read through the Blare alarm clock guide and decided what I wanted my clock to be like. Then I picked the components:
- Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C3 (Just like the guide)
- 3.3V Piezo Buzzer (Just like the guide)
- 0.91 inch 128x32 OLED display

I decided to use capacitive pads as buttons like I've done in previous projects since it means less components, a cheaper BOM, and a slimmer final product.

Then I created the schematic and routed the PCB after importing all the symbol and footprint libraries I needed.

### 2026-10-11 – I changed the main time display. Now, instead of showing the date, time, and status, on different lines, the date and time is shown on the same time, as an ISO 8601 timestamp, making use of the extra

**2h**

I changed the main time display. Now, instead of showing the date, time, and status, on different lines, the date and time is shown on the same time, as an ISO 8601 timestamp, making use of the extra wide display. The status text is shown right below that and I'm only keeping it for now for debugging purposes. Once I get the clock fully functional, I'll probably remove it or make it less obtrusive.

Here's what that looks like in [Lopaka](https://lopaka.app), the site I'm using to test out layouts:
